pl-l2d42c5-d1e108.summary: Notes that sin has various names, peccatum and delictum.

pl-l2d42c5-d1e111.summary: Cites Augustine on Leviticus: delictum is perhaps declining from good, peccatum doing evil; peccatum is perpetrating evil, delictum deserting good, as the name 'derelictum' shows; or delictum is what is done in ignorance, peccatum what is done knowingly; yet each is called by the other's name indifferently.
claims: The terms differ in sense but are interchangeable in use.

pl-l2d42c5.summary: Notes that sin is also called peccatum and delictum. Augustine: delictum is perhaps declining from good, peccatum doing evil; delictum as desertion of good, as the name derelictum shows; or delictum is done in ignorance, peccatum knowingly; yet the terms are used interchangeably.
claims: Delictum may mean deserting good; peccatum doing evil.
Delictum may mean sin in ignorance; peccatum sin knowingly.
The two terms are used interchangeably.
